page: Microsoft Azure E32ps_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine powered by 64-bit ARM architecture using Microsoft Neoverse-N2 processors. It provides 32 dedicated physical cores and 32 vCPUs running at 3.4 GHz with a single thread per core, accompanied by 128 MB of L3 cache. System memory measures 256 GB, resulting in an 8 GB per vCPU allocation ratio. The server features no integrated local storage and contains zero GPUs.

Benchmark measurements indicate exceptional memory subsystem performance. Uncached large-block memory read bandwidth reaches 436.06 GB/sec and write bandwidth reaches 184.19 GB/sec, placing memory throughput in the top tier of cloud servers. These metrics correlate directly with top-tier scores in PassMark database operations and overall memory testing. Multi-core performance is strong across stress-ng multi-core testing, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, and Clang compilation tasks. Single-core performance across Geekbench and stress-ng tests resides within the middle quartile, while large-model LLM prompt processing shows lower throughput.

The 1:8 core-to-memory ratio provides resource density suited for data-heavy operations without hyperthreading overhead. A notable operational tradeoff is the complete reliance on remote attached storage, as no local temporary NVMe storage is provided. The instance is architecturally suited for in-memory databases, Redis caching layers, enterprise relational database servers, and multi-threaded software build systems requiring high memory capacity.
description: Microsoft Azure E32ps_v6 is a memory-optimized cloud server powered by a 32-core ARM Neoverse-N2 processor clocked at 3.4 GHz with dedicated physical core allocation. Providing 256 GB of system RAM, it delivers an 8 GB per vCPU allocation alongside 128 MB of L3 cache, though it includes no local disk storage or GPU accelerators. Benchmark results indicate exceptional uncached memory bandwidth exceeding 436 GB/sec read and 184 GB/sec write speeds, complementing top-tier PassMark database processing capabilities and strong multi-core scaling in compilation and decompression benchmarks. Single-thread performance and large-scale model inference run at average to lower throughput tiers. Due to its high memory density and strong memory throughput, the instance provides qualitative resource efficiency for memory-intensive workloads, including in-memory caching systems, transactional databases, and large-scale multi-threaded compilation workflows requiring extensive RAM.
